paper.title_en: Time-reversal probe of spatially nonuniform information loss in open Rydberg atom arrays
paper.abstract_en: Irreversible quantum information loss is a key issue for understanding nonequilibrium evolution and reliable quantum state preparation in open many-body systems. By using a time-reversal scheme, we investigate spatially nonuniform information loss in a one-dimensional Rydberg atom array. We define defect density operators based on local configurations and use von Neumann entropy together with time reversal to characterize spatially nonuniform irreversible information loss. It is found that central sites exhibit larger single-site von Neumann entropy during the forward evolution, whereas edge sites retain higher residual entropy after the time-reversal. Array parity further affects defect generation, with even-sized arrays exhibiting stronger information loss than odd ones due to geometric frustration. The interplay between nonadiabatic excitations and dissipation during the detuning sweep is analyzed. An optimal sweep rate is identified to minimize defect formation in the dynamic process. These results provide a spatially resolved perspective for understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics and optimize the state preparation in open Rydberg atom arrays. •Time reversal probes irreversible information loss in Rydberg atom arrays.•Boundary constraints shape the spatial distribution of local mixedness.•Residual entropy probes spatially nonuniform irreversible information loss.•Interplay between nonadiabatic excitations and dissipation governs defect generation.
